chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a menstruating woman handing water to a man. He said: “Some of the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to pour water over him while she was menstruating, and she would hand him the khumrah.”

key_terms.الْحَائِضِ: a woman in the state of menstruation
key_terms.الْخُمْرَةَ: a small mat or cloth used for sajdah or sitting
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, here in the context of personal use or purification

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman hand water or objects to a man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that a menstruating woman may hand water or other items to a man, and that her state of menstruation does not prevent such contact or service. The Imam عليه السلام supports this ruling by citing the practice of some of the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
